name: Exxon Mobil

points.text: Revenue is growing 32.6% year over year (strong).
Earnings jumped +111% versus a year ago, but that mostly reflects a depressed prior year.
Operating margin is 12.9%.
Return on equity is 15.5%.
Debt/equity is 13% (conservative leverage).
Free-cash-flow margin is 7.3% of revenue.
It trades at 12.8x forward earnings.
PEG ratio is 1.24 (price paid per unit of growth).
EV/EBITDA is 8.6x.
Free-cash-flow yield is 4.4%.
Price is 2.7% above its 200-day average: the long-term trend is up.
The 50-day average is above the 200-day average (bullish alignment).
RSI(14) is 38: sellers in control.
MACD is negative but improving.
It is 14.4% below its 52-week high.
22 Wall Street analysts rate it 2.4/5 on average (buy).
The average analyst price target implies 15.7% upside.
Over 6 months it returned +9.7% versus -1.7% for the MSCI World benchmark.
It fell 10.9% in the last month.
Annualised volatility is 27%.
Worst peak-to-trough fall in the past year: 20.1%.
Beta of 0.14: defensive, moves less than the market.
No exposure to Energy yet — this would diversify the portfolio.

debate.said: Here is the case for owning Exxon Mobil. Revenue is growing 32.6% year over year (strong). Price is 2.7% above its 200-day average: the long-term trend is up. Over 6 months it returned +9.7% versus -1.7% for the MSCI World benchmark.
I'm not convinced. RSI(14) is 38: sellers in control. It fell 10.9% in the last month. MACD is negative but improving.
Price action is noise over a few weeks; the business is what we own — revenue is growing 32.6% year over year (strong). Weakness can be an entry point.

risk: Maximum position size: 16% of the portfolio (scaled for 27% volatility).
Every order costs a €1 fee, like on Trade Republic. Stop-loss rule: review at -15% from cost.
chair: Weighted committee score is +0.26 on a scale of -1 to +1; 5 of 5 analysts lean the same way. Conviction: Medium.
Decision: BUY. We propose a position of up to 16% of the portfolio.
